You're working on Nxeon, a VPS/game-server hosting platform. Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript. Production repo: /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`).

## Context: this is a redo

A prior attempt at this exact task shipped on branch `feature/singapore-redesign` (commit `854754f`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps`, new files under `components/marketing/singapore/`). The owner reviewed it and rejected it: **"this is not an overhaul... a fresh overhaul... don't use any context from Nxeon's previous styling from other pages."** It was too visually conservative — it kept the platform's navy/violet/cyan palette and generally read as a variation on the existing look, not a genuine departure. You are doing this again, properly.

**Do not reuse or lightly edit the previous attempt's visual design.** You may look at `git show 854754f` purely to understand the technical pattern (how the page was decoupled from the shared template, build/verification steps), but the color palette, typography, layout rhythm, and motion language from that attempt must NOT carry into this one. Treat this as if you're designing for a brand-new product that happens to need this one page.

## First step — isolate yourself

Never build or run dev servers in the live `/opt/nxeon` tree. Start a fresh worktree off `main` (not off the old branch — this is a clean creative reset):
```
cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps2 -b feature/singapore-redesign-v2
cd /opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps2
ln -sfn /opt/nxeon/node_modules node_modules
ln -sf /opt/nxeon/.env .env
```
Do all your work in `/opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps2`.

## The page

Target: `https://nxeon.cloud/singapore-vps-hosting`, source `app/(marketing)/singapore-vps-hosting/page.tsx`. It currently renders `<UseCaseLanding content={...}>` from `components/marketing/UseCaseLanding.tsx` — a shared template used by 13 other pages. **Hard constraint, non-negotiable: do not modify `UseCaseLanding.tsx` or any other shared component in a way that affects the other 13 pages.** This page becomes fully bespoke — its own component tree, used only here. Before you finish, run `grep -rl "UseCaseLanding" "app/(marketing)"` and confirm nothing else was touched.

## What's being torn down (the actual current page, described exactly — this is the "before," not a style reference)

Dark navy background throughout. A pill badge reading "SINGAPORE DATACENTER" in small caps. A large headline: "A Singapore VPS built for" in white, then "Asia-Pacific" as a second line in a violet-to-cyan gradient. Below it, sub-copy and two buttons (a violet-to-cyan gradient filled button "Deploy now", and an outlined "See pricing"). To the right of the hero text, a two-part visual: a small card reading "sgp1 · Singapore · Live" with a spec list (vCPU/Memory/Storage/Bandwidth/IPv4/Uptime) and a "Deploying your server... 47s... 100%... SSH ready" progress bar, sitting beside a dark world/APAC map graphic with small dots for Singapore/Japan/Vietnam/Indonesia/Australia and thin animated arcing lines pulsing between them. Below the hero: a row of 6 small feature cards with line-icons (Low latency, Enterprise NVMe, Full root access, DDoS protection, Instant deployment, 24/7 support). Then a "Pick your Singapore VPS" section: 4 pricing cards side by side (Starter/Standard/Pro/Max), each with a price, a bulleted spec list, and a "Deploy now" button, one marked "MOST POPULAR" with a violet badge and violet-tinted border. Then a two-column block: a latency-by-country table on the left (Singapore/Malaysia/Indonesia/Thailand/Vietnam/India/Australia/Japan with ms figures and "Test now" links) and an "Everything included" icon checklist on the right. Then a horizontal "Deploy in 47 seconds" 3-step strip (numbered circles). Then a 2-column FAQ accordion. Then a CTA banner with a 3D-rendered server/box graphic, "Your Singapore VPS is 47 seconds away," and buttons. All of it: dark navy everywhere, the same violet-to-cyan gradient repeated on every accent, the same card style (rounded corners, thin border, subtle glow) repeated in every section. **This exact look — the palette, the gradient-text trick, the map-with-pulsing-lines motif, the card style, the section rhythm — is precisely what must not survive into the new version.**

## What "fresh overhaul" actually means here

Pick ONE real, specific creative direction for this page and commit to it fully — not "modern dark SaaS with a different accent color." Ground it in the actual subject: this is a low-latency VPS hosted in Singapore for Asia-Pacific developers/businesses. Real directions that would count as genuinely different (these are illustrative, not prescriptive — choose your own, but it must be this concrete and specific, not a vibe):
- A network-diagnostics/oscilloscope instrument aesthetic: monospace type, scan-line motion, real-time-feeling readouts, a genuinely different color language (e.g. phosphor green on near-black, or amber terminal tones) instead of violet/cyan gradients.
- An editorial/print-inspired layout: bold serif or condensed-grotesk display type, asymmetric grid, large negative space, a restrained 2-color palette, motion used sparingly as punctuation rather than ambient decoration.
- A physical/cartographic direction: treat "Singapore, the physical place" as the hero subject — real geographic/timezone framing, a genuinely different way of visualizing distance/latency than a dotted world map with arcs.

Whatever you pick, it needs its own type pairing (not necessarily whatever font the rest of the site uses — check what's already loaded via next/font or Google Fonts in `app/layout.tsx`/`globals.css`, and feel free to add a new one if it serves the direction, as long as it's a real font source, e.g. next/font/google), its own palette (name 4-6 actual hex values as your token set, don't just reach for the existing navy/violet/cyan tokens in `app/globals.css`), and its own motion language built specifically for this page — not a re-skin of the pulsing-map trick.

Avoid generic AI-design tells: no default Inter-on-dark-navy-with-a-gradient-word, no identical rounded-card-with-glow repeated in every section, no centered-everything, no emoji as icons, no the-same-two-colors-on-every-accent. If what you're building would look at home as a generic SaaS template with the words swapped out, it's not different enough — go back and commit harder to the direction you picked.

## Real data — don't invent numbers

Pull actual plan pricing/specs from wherever the current `content: UseCaseContent` object in `app/(marketing)/singapore-vps-hosting/page.tsx` sources it (check for a live plans/pricing data file under `lib/` — the previous attempt found the hero's advertised price was stale vs. the live DB, so verify against the real source, not the old page's hardcoded copy). Real numbers only: pricing, specs, uptime, latency, deploy time. No fabricated testimonials/review counts — check the DB/codebase for anything genuinely available before including social proof.

## Motion graphics

No baz this time — skip it entirely, don't invoke that skill. Build real motion in code: CSS/SVG/Canvas/WebGL, whatever the direction calls for. Check `package.json` for what's already available (Framer Motion, GSAP, Three.js) before adding anything new; if you add a dependency, prove `npm run build` still passes with it. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. The previous attempt's motion (a rotating radar sweep over a map) should not reappear here even in disguised form — build something that serves your new direction specifically.

## Scope boundaries

The global header (`MarketingHeader.tsx`) and footer (`MarketingFooter.tsx`) are shared site-wide chrome — leave them untouched, out of scope; a visitor should still recognize they're on nxeon.cloud from the nav/footer even though the page body looks like nothing else on the site. Keep `export const metadata` in `page.tsx` accurate.

## Build safety / verification

Run `npm run build` in `/opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps2` to confirm it compiles. If Playwright (or similar) is in devDependencies, screenshot the finished page at 1440px and 390px widths — scroll through if any reveals are scroll-triggered — so you can actually see what you built before calling it done. Save screenshots somewhere you'll reference in your report.

## Stop condition

Do not merge to main, do not touch staging or production. Commit on `feature/singapore-redesign-v2` in `/opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps2` and stop. Report: the specific creative direction you chose and why it fits the subject (this is the part that proves it's not generic), the commit hash, how to preview it, and screenshot paths.

## Summary

**Creative direction: "The Meridian Chart"** — an aeronautical/maritime navigation-chart instrument aesthetic. Rationale: Nxeon's Singapore VPS is fundamentally a claim about *physical geography* (a real datacenter, sold on real distance to APAC users), so the page treats "Singapore as a place" as the actual subject — a plotting sheet, compass, range table, and deploy log — rather than another dark-SaaS gradient page. This is one of the three illustrative directions from the brief (physical/cartographic), pushed to a specific, fully-committed execution, not a vibe.

- **Palette** (all new, no navy/violet/cyan): `#f2ecdd` paper, `#e7dfc7` panel paper, `#1e2a22` ink, `#4b5a4e` soft ink, `#c9bd9c` hairline rule, `#c1440e` vermillion (CTAs/course lines), `#8a6a2f` brass (ticks/stamps).
- **Type**: Fraunces (serif display, headlines/pull-quotes) + IBM Plex Mono (all data/coordinates/labels) — loaded via `next/font/google`, scoped to this route only, never touching the site's Geist tokens.
- **Motion**: a compass needle that settles once (not spinning), hand-drawn rhumb-lines from Singapore to each city that draw themselves in via `stroke-dashoffset`, count-up distance odometers, and a sweeping instrument dial for the "deploy in 47s" sequence — no radar sweep, no ambient pulsing. All respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Real data only**: live plan pricing from `db.plan` ($8.88–$32.99, replacing the old page's stale $6.49), and a haversine-computed distance/bearing/UTC-offset table to 9 regional cities from Singapore's real coordinates — replacing the old page's invented per-country millisecond latency numbers. No fabricated testimonials (none exist in the DB).

**Technical isolation**: fully bespoke component tree under `app/(marketing)/singapore-vps-hosting/_components/` (route-local, excluded from routing), scoped by `chart.module.css`. `UseCaseLanding.tsx` and the other 13 pages using it are untouched (verified via `grep -rl "import.*UseCaseLanding"`, still exactly 12 other files). Header/footer untouched.

**Bug found and fixed along the way**: the reveal-on-scroll effect used a `clip-path` wipe, and Chromium computes `IntersectionObserver`'s `intersectionRatio` against the *clipped* (near-zero) area rather than the layout box, so a ratio-based threshold (0.15) silently never fired. Switched to `threshold: 0`, which reacts to the `isIntersecting` boolean (unaffected by clip-path) — documented inline in `RevealChart.tsx` so it doesn't get "fixed" back incorrectly later.
